open_obligations: Note that in recursive reward modeling the assisting task differs from the trained task.
Check whether training with reward modeling changes failure modes relative to learning from Amplify_H(X).
Check whether either proposal had experiments with human decomposers.
in.other_title: Recursive reward modeling: agent A(k-1) assists the user in evaluating agent A(k)
in.rationale: Christiano et al. define Amplify_H(X), a human plus copies of the current agent, as the system the agent learns from in the same way it would learn from H alone. Leike et al. define recursive reward modeling, where A(k-1) assists the user in evaluating outcomes when training A(k). Neither cited passage refers to the other scheme, so the passages show two schemes for the same problem in different settings rather than one building on the other.
in.scope: proposed SAME_QUESTION_DIFFERENT_SETTING: recursive schemes where agents help a human train an agent, with copies of the current agent helping a human expert in Christiano et al. and the previous agent helping the user evaluate outcomes under reward modeling in Leike et al.; Christiano et al. focus on question-answering tasks, while Leike et al. train agents on tasks whose outcomes the user evaluates

text: The authors define Amplify_H(X) as the composite system in which a human expert H invokes several copies of the current agent X to help solve a problem; X then learns from Amplify_H(X) the same way it would traditionally learn from H alone. In this paper the task set is question answering.
title: Amplify_H(X): human expert plus copies of the current agent as the training target
